findings.problem: Contract-vs-code divergence inside signal C's sub-signals. The frozen contract's C2 is 'distinct action verbs (add|build|change|check|implement|verify|设计|实现|验证|改造|补充) >= 3', but session-start.js::ACTION_VERB_PATTERN also counts align|consolidate|migrate|overhaul|port|refactor|rewrite (CLAUSE_ACTION_PATTERN has the same wider set). Measured difference that matters: frozen complex prompt #1 yields C2=2 under the contract list (so the contract's literal C would not fire) but C2=3 under the shipped list — which is the only reason that prompt triggers at all; the contract's logicRevisionNote justifies Option A by the frozen complex prompts being unreachable under >=2, a justification that holds only because C2 was widened. Code and contract now agree on the trigger threshold but still disagree on what counts as C2/C3, and the two-sided case cannot see it because it pins the same wide list on both sides.
findings.requiredFix: Amend the frozen contract's C2/C3 verb lists to the implemented set (add align|consolidate|migrate|overhaul|port|refactor|rewrite), recording that the widened list is what makes frozen complex #1 reachable; or narrow ACTION_VERB_PATTERN/CLAUSE_ACTION_PATTERN to the contract list and accept that complex #1 then needs its prompt revised. Prefer the amendment (the behaviour is ratified); never change only one side. Documentation scope — no behaviour change required.

residualRisks: Option A's accepted cost is a precision dial on the only automatic trigger: a single satisfied C (or a single B, or a single D) now admits the gate. The ordinary-prompt trigger RATE under >=1 is unmeasured anywhere in this wave; it is the one open acceptance-cost item I would not close without a small calibration corpus of prompts expected to stay solo.

The frozen two-sided case cannot see this class: it pins exactly the 3+3 prompt sets (which pass) plus a disarmed control, so neither an over-eager trigger nor the C2 divergence is observable through it. A calibration corpus is the missing falsifier.

The live-model half of R4 (the model builds a team itself and the plugin must not add a second) is structural only: session-start provisioning returns early when the session already leads a team, and the duplicate case proves the one-team invariant in the model-incapable path, but no live-model turn exists in this environment to exercise it end to end.
Browser rendering is unexercised in both directions (F2 panel parity and the R4 inquiry text) — asserted at the data/view layer and in session logs only.

The R4 deterministic trigger depends on the ambient deployment answering MISSING_CREDENTIAL as it does today; if a future sandbox gains a model route, the happy case would stop proving plugin-side staging and would need a tool-denied or model-disabled configuration.

closureVerdict.statement: The wave's three user-facing goals are delivered and independently verified: a session no longer starts inside a team by default (gated auto-route; frozen 3+3 passing both ways; a disarmed reverse control proving the gate is not a tautological path), a failed dependency no longer blocks its dependent AND the panel/contract views agree about it, and an explicit team request is now deterministic (plugin-side staged team in a model-incapable environment, ask-first on an existing unapproved team, visible warning on a disabled command surface, explicit error on an unknown profile, with a dedicated QA case covering all four). F3 (the overwritten verification report) was closed by reconstruction and re-verified by me; F1's threshold contradiction was closed by the captain's contract amendment; the remaining open items are documentation/declaration hygiene (F1-SUB medium, F2-LOW..F5-LOW) plus the unmeasured trigger-rate acceptance cost, none of which blocks the delivered behaviour.
